stem: A developer wants to manage AWS resources by running repeatable commands and shell scripts from a laptop terminal. Which tool should the developer use?
explanation: The AWS CLI issues AWS API calls as terminal commands that can be scripted and repeated. The Management Console is a browser-based point-and-click interface, so it is not suited to scripting.

stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which task is the company's responsibility?
options: Maintaining the physical hosts in the data center
Patching the hypervisor that runs the instances
Replacing failed storage hardware in the Region
explanation: EC2 is infrastructure as a service, so the customer patches and secures the guest operating system and everything above it. The hypervisor, host hardware and facilities are security of the cloud, which AWS owns.

stem: A company wants to stop guessing how many servers it will need for a product launch next quarter. Which advantage of cloud computing does this describe?
options: Benefit from massive economies of scale
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
explanation: In the cloud a company provisions what it needs and scales up or down with demand, so it no longer has to forecast capacity in advance. Economies of scale lower prices, but they do not remove the need to forecast server counts.

stem: A company runs a database server on EC2 around the clock with a stable, predictable load for the next three years. It will not change instance families. Which purchasing option gives the lowest cost?
explanation: A 3-year Standard Reserved Instance gives the deepest RI discount (up to 72%) for steady, predictable usage. Convertible RIs and shorter terms discount less, and Spot Instances can be interrupted, which a database cannot tolerate.

stem: A company wants to provision identical development, test and production environments repeatedly from version-controlled JSON or YAML templates. Which AWS service meets this need?
explanation: CloudFormation is infrastructure as code: a template in JSON or YAML defines resources that are created the same way every time as a stack. AWS Config records and evaluates resource configurations but does not provision them.

stem: A company moves its relational database to Amazon RDS. Which task remains the company's responsibility under the shared responsibility model?
options: Managing database user accounts and permissions
Applying operating system patches to the database host
explanation: On RDS, AWS patches the database engine and host operating system and maintains the hardware. The customer still controls who can access the database, including database users, IAM access and network rules.

stem: A company wants to replace large upfront hardware purchases with monthly payments based only on what it actually uses. Which advantage of cloud computing applies?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
explanation: Paying only for consumed resources turns capital expenditure on hardware into variable operating expense. Stopping spending on data centers is a related advantage, but it describes freeing staff from facility work, not the CapEx-to-OpEx pricing shift.

stem: Developers on a team prefer to define cloud infrastructure in familiar programming languages such as TypeScript and Python instead of templates. Which AWS offering supports this?
explanation: The CDK lets developers model infrastructure as code in general-purpose languages and synthesizes it into CloudFormation templates. An AWS SDK calls service APIs from application code but is not an infrastructure-as-code framework.

stem: Which statement best summarizes the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: AWS secures all customer data once any support plan is purchased
Customers secure hardware; AWS secures customer data
AWS and customers split every security control equally
AWS secures the cloud; customers secure what they put in it
explanation: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud (infrastructure, hardware, facilities), while customers are responsible for security IN the cloud (data, identities, configuration). No support plan transfers data protection to AWS.

stem: Why is AWS able to offer lower pay-as-you-go prices than most companies could achieve by running their own data centers?
options: Aggregated usage from many customers creates economies of scale
Each customer receives dedicated physical hardware
Customers pay for reserved capacity instead of usage
Customers are responsible for maintaining the physical data center facilities
explanation: Because AWS aggregates usage from hundreds of thousands of customers, it achieves higher economies of scale and passes the savings on as lower prices. Customers never maintain AWS facilities; physical security and maintenance are AWS's responsibility.

stem: A team wants to upload its Java web application code and let AWS automatically handle capacity provisioning, load balancing, scaling and health monitoring. Which service should the team use?
options: Amazon EC2 with manually configured instances
explanation: Elastic Beanstalk is a platform service: you upload code and it deploys and manages the underlying EC2, load balancing and Auto Scaling for you. CloudFormation can build the same resources but you must define and manage every one yourself.

stem: A developer deploys application code to AWS Lambda. Which responsibility remains with the developer rather than with AWS?
options: Patching the operating system that runs functions
Scaling the physical compute fleet behind Lambda
Maintaining the runtime hosts in each Availability Zone
Securing the function code and its IAM permissions
explanation: With Lambda, AWS manages the servers, operating system, runtime patching and scaling. The customer remains responsible for its own code, the data it handles and the IAM permissions granted to the function.

stem: A company wants a Reserved Instance discount but expects to switch instance families and operating systems during the term. Which option should it purchase?
explanation: Convertible Reserved Instances can be exchanged for RIs with a different instance family, operating system or tenancy. Standard RIs offer a larger discount but cannot be exchanged for a different instance family.

stem: Which statement best describes a hybrid cloud deployment model?
options: All workloads running entirely in AWS Regions
On-premises infrastructure connected to resources running in AWS
All workloads running in a private on-premises data center
Workloads spread across multiple Availability Zones in one Region
explanation: A hybrid deployment links existing on-premises infrastructure with cloud resources, often over VPN or Direct Connect. Running everything in AWS, even across several Availability Zones, is a cloud (cloud-native) deployment.

stem: A company wants its developers to experiment with new ideas by launching test environments in minutes and discarding them cheaply. Which cloud benefit does this represent?
explanation: Agility means resources are available in minutes, so the cost and time of experimenting drops sharply. High availability is about keeping workloads running during failures, not about how fast teams can try new ideas.

stem: A company stores confidential documents in Amazon S3. Which security task is the company responsible for?
options: Replicating objects across multiple devices for durability
Securing storage hardware inside AWS facilities
Configuring bucket policies and Block Public Access
Destroying disks that once held customer data
explanation: Access control on buckets and objects is security in the cloud, so the customer configures bucket policies and Block Public Access. Durability, storage hardware and media destruction are handled by AWS.

stem: A financial firm needs a dedicated private network connection from its data center to AWS with consistent bandwidth that does not travel over the public internet. Which service should it use?
explanation: Direct Connect provides a dedicated private link between a data center and AWS with more consistent performance than the internet. A Site-to-Site VPN is encrypted but still travels over the public internet.

stem: A company wants its ticketing website to add servers automatically during sudden demand spikes and remove them when demand drops. Which cloud concept is this?
explanation: Elasticity is the ability to acquire resources as demand rises and release them as it falls, typically with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling. Fault tolerance keeps a system running when components fail, which is a different goal.

stem: The AWS shared responsibility model lists some controls as shared, applied by AWS to its layer and by the customer to its own. Which controls are shared? (Choose three.)
explanation: AWS names patch management, configuration management, and awareness and training as shared controls: AWS handles its infrastructure and staff, and customers handle their own systems and people. Physical and environmental security is tempting because it protects every workload, but it is an inherited control that AWS alone provides, as are data center access logging and media disposal.

stem: A branch office needs an encrypted connection to its Amazon VPC that can be set up within hours using its existing internet link. Which option is most appropriate?
explanation: A Site-to-Site VPN creates IPsec-encrypted tunnels over the existing internet connection and can be set up quickly at low cost. Direct Connect requires a physical circuit that typically takes weeks to provision.

stem: A company runs workloads on Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda and AWS Fargate and wants one flexible commitment that discounts all three. Which pricing model fits?
explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2 in any family or Region, Lambda and Fargate in exchange for a 1- or 3-year hourly spend commitment. EC2 Instance Savings Plans give a bigger discount but cover only one instance family in one Region and do not cover Lambda or Fargate.

stem: A mobile app developer wants application code written in Java to read and write objects in Amazon S3 and items in DynamoDB directly. What should the developer use?
explanation: AWS SDKs provide language-specific libraries that let application code call AWS APIs programmatically. The CLI also calls the APIs, but from a terminal rather than from inside the application's own code.

stem: How does the AWS shared responsibility model handle security awareness and training?
options: AWS trains every customer employee on security at no charge
AWS trains its employees; customers train their own employees
Customers must train AWS data center staff
Only AWS Partners may deliver security training
explanation: Awareness and training is a shared control: each party applies it within its own scope, so AWS trains AWS staff and customers train their own people. AWS does not take over customer staff training.

stem: A company wants to serve customers in Asia and Europe with low latency within days, without building any new data centers. Which cloud advantage is this?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explanation: AWS Regions around the world let a company deploy close to customers in a few clicks. Stop guessing capacity is about sizing infrastructure, not about geographic reach.

stem: A company is choosing the AWS Region for a new application. Which factors should it consider? (Choose three.)
options: Number of IAM users in the account
explanation: Region choice is driven by compliance and data residency, proximity to users for low latency, service availability and pricing. The number of edge locations is tempting because edge locations reduce latency, but the edge network is global and the same whichever Region is chosen, and IAM and Support plans apply to the whole account.

stem: A company runs containers on Amazon ECS and is deciding between EC2 instances and AWS Fargate. How does choosing Fargate change its responsibilities?
options: The company must now patch the host kernel
AWS becomes responsible for container image code
The company no longer needs IAM permissions
AWS manages and patches the underlying servers
explanation: Fargate is serverless compute for containers, so AWS provisions, patches and scales the underlying hosts. The customer still owns its container images, application code and IAM configuration.

stem: A team is reviewing its workload against the reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework. Which design principles belong to this pillar? (Choose three.)
explanation: Automatically recovering from failure, testing recovery procedures and scaling horizontally to increase aggregate availability are reliability design principles. Using serverless architectures sounds resilient, but it is a performance efficiency principle; a strong identity foundation belongs to security and attributing expenditure to cost optimization.

stem: A company's web application must remain available if a single data center fails. Which architecture provides this high availability at the lowest complexity?
options: EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones behind a load balancer
Larger EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone
One EC2 instance in a Local Zone
Content cached at multiple edge locations
explanation: Each Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with independent power and networking, so spreading instances across AZs behind a load balancer survives a data center failure. A bigger instance in one AZ is still a single point of failure.

stem: A company wants to cut Amazon EC2 costs with Spot Instances. Which workloads are good candidates? (Choose two.)
explanation: Spot Instances can be reclaimed with a two-minute warning, so they suit flexible, interruption-tolerant work such as rendering batches and stateless build workers. A long job that cannot checkpoint looks like a cheap batch job, but one interruption throws away all of its progress, and databases and checkout services need steady capacity.

stem: A company's security officer asks who protects the data center buildings that host the company's Amazon EC2 instances. What is the correct answer?
options: The AWS Partner that resells the account
explanation: Physical and environmental security of AWS facilities is entirely AWS's responsibility under the shared responsibility model. Customers never manage data center access, whatever service they use.

stem: Which term describes a system's ability to handle a growing workload by adding resources, such as more instances or storage?
explanation: Scalability is the ability to grow to meet increased load, either by adding instances or by using larger ones. Durability refers to protecting stored data from loss, not to handling more workload.

stem: A healthcare provider is legally required to keep patient records stored within its own country. What should it consider first when designing its AWS deployment?
options: Choosing an edge location inside that country
Enabling AWS Global Accelerator for the application
Spreading data across multiple Availability Zones
Choosing an AWS Region located in that country
explanation: Data stored in a Region stays in that Region unless the customer moves it, so Region choice is how data residency is met. Edge locations cache content for delivery and are not where a company chooses to store its primary data.

stem: A company stores application data in Amazon DynamoDB. Under the shared responsibility model, which tasks does AWS handle? (Choose two.)
options: Writing IAM policies for the tables
Classifying the data in the tables
explanation: DynamoDB is fully managed, so AWS patches the underlying servers and replaces failed hardware. Point-in-time recovery is tempting because it is a DynamoDB backup feature, but the customer must choose to turn it on, just as it writes IAM policies and classifies its own data.

stem: A startup wants to run code without provisioning or managing servers. Which AWS compute services are serverless? (Choose two.)
explanation: Lambda runs functions and Fargate runs containers without any servers for the customer to provision, patch or scale. Lightsail is tempting because it is simple to use, but it still gives you a virtual server that you size and maintain.

stem: A company wants its IT staff to build customer features instead of racking servers and managing power and cooling. Which cloud advantage applies?
options: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
explanation: AWS handles the heavy lifting of racking, stacking, and powering servers, so staff can focus on customers. Speed and agility is related but describes how quickly resources can be provisioned, not removing facility work.

stem: A company stores sensitive data on Amazon EBS volumes attached to EC2 instances. Who is responsible for enabling encryption of that data at rest?
options: AWS Support, once a support plan exists
The AWS compliance team through AWS Artifact
explanation: Protecting customer data, including choosing to encrypt EBS volumes with KMS keys, is the customer's responsibility. AWS provides the encryption feature, but the customer must enable and manage it.

stem: A company must bring existing server-bound software licenses priced per physical core and socket to AWS. Which EC2 option provides that visibility?
explanation: Dedicated Hosts give a whole physical server with visibility into sockets and cores, which bring-your-own-license terms often require. Dedicated Instances also run on single-tenant hardware but give no control over or visibility into the underlying host.

stem: An online gaming company runs a UDP-based application and wants fixed static IP addresses that route players over the AWS global network to the healthiest regional endpoint. Which service fits best?
options: Network Load Balancer in one Region
explanation: Global Accelerator provides two static anycast IP addresses and sends TCP or UDP traffic across the AWS backbone to the optimal healthy endpoint. CloudFront is designed for caching HTTP content, not for non-HTTP gaming traffic with static IPs.

stem: A company moving to AWS wants to know which security benefit it gains automatically for the physical infrastructure. Which statement is correct?
options: AWS patches the guest operating systems on all EC2 instances
AWS configures the customer's security group rules
AWS manages permissions for the customer's IAM users
AWS secures the data centers, hardware, and global network
explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS is responsible for security of the cloud: facilities, hardware, and network infrastructure. Patching the guest operating system on EC2 remains the customer's job.

stem: Which responsibility belongs to AWS for every AWS service, regardless of whether it is infrastructure, container or managed?
options: Configuring the security group rules for customer instances
Protecting the infrastructure that runs the services
explanation: AWS always protects the global infrastructure: hardware, software, networking and facilities that run AWS services. Security groups, IAM credentials and data encryption choices remain customer tasks.

stem: A telecommunications partner wants to deploy applications for 5G mobile devices with ultra-low latency by running compute inside carrier networks. Which AWS offering is designed for this?
explanation: Wavelength Zones embed AWS compute and storage within telecom providers' 5G networks so traffic does not leave the carrier network. Local Zones place AWS infrastructure near large cities but not inside carrier 5G networks.

stem: A company runs a reporting workload only during the last three days of each month. Which cloud benefit lowers its cost most directly?
options: Pay-as-you-go pricing for resources actually used
Global reach through hundreds of CloudFront edge locations
Eleven nines of durability in Amazon S3
explanation: With pay-as-you-go pricing the company pays only while the reporting resources run and can shut them down for the rest of the month. Multi-AZ deployment improves availability but adds cost rather than removing it.

stem: A company replaces self-managed MySQL on Amazon EC2 with Amazon RDS for MySQL. Which responsibility moves from the company to AWS?
options: Controlling which users can query the data
Installing database engine and OS patches
Encrypting sensitive columns in the application
Restricting network access to the database port
explanation: Moving to RDS hands database engine and operating system patching to AWS. User access, application-level encryption and security group rules stay with the customer.

stem: A manufacturer must run AWS services inside its own factory data center for low-latency access to local systems, using the same AWS APIs and tools. Which service should it choose?
explanation: Outposts delivers AWS-managed racks or servers into the customer's own facility, running AWS services with the same APIs. Local Zones are AWS-operated sites near population centers, not hardware installed on the customer's premises.

stem: A retailer needs guaranteed EC2 capacity in one Availability Zone for a two-week sales event and wants no long-term commitment. Which option should it use?
explanation: On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve capacity in a specific Availability Zone for any duration and can be cancelled at any time. Savings Plans lower the price but do not reserve capacity, and they require a 1- or 3-year commitment.

stem: A film studio in a large city far from the nearest AWS Region needs single-digit millisecond latency for rendering workstations without installing hardware on site. Which option should it use?
explanation: Local Zones extend a Region with AWS-operated compute and storage close to large metropolitan areas for very low latency. Outposts would also give low latency, but it requires installing AWS hardware in the studio's own facility.

stem: A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2. Who is responsible for configuring the security group rules that control inbound traffic to the instances?
options: AWS Managed Services, for every account
explanation: Network and firewall configuration, including security group rules, is security in the cloud and belongs to the customer. AWS provides the feature but does not decide which traffic a workload should allow.

stem: Which statements correctly describe AWS Availability Zones? (Choose two.)
options: One or more discrete data centers
Each located in a different country
Share one power source per Region
explanation: An Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with redundant power and networking, and the AZs in a Region are connected by low-latency, high-bandwidth links. Caching CloudFront content is tempting because it also improves performance, but that is the job of edge locations; the AZs of a Region sit in the same geographic area, not in different countries.

stem: A company runs nightly image-processing jobs that can be stopped and restarted at any time without harm. Which EC2 purchasing option is most cost-effective?
explanation: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at up to 90% off and suit interruption-tolerant workloads. On-Demand works but costs far more for jobs that can tolerate being interrupted.

stem: A company must make sure data sent from users' browsers to its application on AWS is encrypted. Who is responsible for configuring that encryption in transit?
options: AWS, which encrypts all traffic automatically
AWS Shield, which encrypts web requests
The customer, for example by enforcing TLS
The edge location operators in each Region
explanation: Network traffic protection for a customer's application is the customer's responsibility, typically by using HTTPS with TLS certificates. AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks and does not encrypt traffic.

stem: A company wants to run and monitor systems, make frequent small reversible changes, and learn from operational failures. Which Well-Architected pillar is this?
explanation: Operational excellence covers running and monitoring systems, performing operations as code, and making frequent, small, reversible changes. Reliability focuses on recovering from failures and meeting demand, not on improving operational procedures.

stem: Which workloads are best suited to Amazon EC2 compute optimized instances? (Choose two.)
explanation: Compute optimized instances have a high ratio of CPU to memory for compute-bound work such as high performance web servers, dedicated gaming servers, batch processing and media transcoding. GPU model training sounds compute heavy, but it runs on accelerated computing instances; in-memory databases suit memory optimized and local-disk warehouses storage optimized instances.

stem: A company is estimating the hourly price of an On-Demand Amazon EC2 instance. Which factors change that price? (Choose two.)
explanation: On-Demand EC2 prices depend on the instance type and size, the Region and the operating system. The Support plan is tempting because it is also an AWS charge, but it is billed separately and does not change an instance's hourly rate.

stem: A startup wants to minimize the infrastructure it must secure, patch and manage. Which compute option shifts the most responsibility to AWS?
explanation: With Lambda, AWS manages servers, operating systems, runtimes and scaling, leaving the customer mainly its code and permissions. EC2 instances, Dedicated Hosts and Outposts all leave the guest operating system to the customer.

stem: An analytics application processes very large datasets entirely in RAM and needs a high ratio of memory to vCPU. Which EC2 instance family should be chosen?
explanation: Memory optimized instances are built for workloads that process large datasets in memory, such as in-memory databases and analytics. Compute optimized instances favor high CPU performance relative to memory.

stem: Which Well-Architected pillar includes the design principles of implementing a strong identity foundation and enabling traceability?
explanation: A strong identity foundation, traceability, and applying security at all layers are design principles of the security pillar. Operational excellence includes observability, but identity and traceability for protection belong to security.

stem: A company's external auditors request a copy of the AWS SOC 2 report. Which AWS service should the company use to download it?
explanation: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for AWS compliance reports such as SOC, PCI and ISO, plus agreements like the BAA. Audit Manager collects evidence about the customer's own usage, not AWS's reports.

stem: Traffic to a news website spikes unpredictably during breaking stories. Which service automatically adds EC2 instances during spikes and removes them when demand drops?
explanation: EC2 Auto Scaling launches and terminates instances to match demand, which provides elasticity. CloudWatch supplies the metrics and alarms that can trigger scaling, but it does not launch instances by itself.

stem: A company wants its workload to recover automatically from infrastructure failures and to perform its intended function consistently. Which pillar addresses this?
explanation: The reliability pillar covers automatically recovering from failure, testing recovery procedures, and scaling horizontally. Performance efficiency is about using resources efficiently, not about recovering from failures.

stem: A company wants to continuously and automatically collect evidence from its own AWS usage to prepare for a PCI DSS audit. Which service should it use?
explanation: Audit Manager maps a customer's AWS usage to frameworks like PCI DSS and gathers audit-ready evidence automatically. Artifact only provides AWS's own compliance reports and agreements.

stem: A company runs several microservices and needs to route HTTPS requests to different targets based on the URL path, such as /api or /images. Which load balancer type should it use?
explanation: An Application Load Balancer works at layer 7 and supports path-based and host-based routing for HTTP and HTTPS. A Network Load Balancer works at layer 4 and cannot inspect URL paths.

stem: A company is estimating the network charges for a new web application. Which type of data transfer is generally free of charge?
options: Data transferred into AWS from the internet
Data transferred out of AWS to the internet
Data transferred between two AWS Regions
explanation: Inbound data transfer from the internet is generally not charged. Outbound transfer to the internet, cross-Region transfer and most cross-AZ transfer are billed per GB.

stem: A company wants to select the most suitable resource types, adopt serverless architectures, and experiment more often as requirements change. Which pillar applies?
explanation: Performance efficiency focuses on using computing resources efficiently, including serverless architectures, democratizing advanced technologies, and experimenting more often. Cost optimization also involves choosing resources, but its goal is the lowest price rather than meeting performance requirements.

stem: A security team must find out which IAM user deleted an Amazon S3 bucket last week. Which AWS service records this information?
explanation: CloudTrail records API calls, including who made the call, from where and when, so it answers who deleted the bucket. CloudWatch tracks metrics and logs for performance, not an audit of API activity.

stem: A photo-sharing app must create a thumbnail whenever a user uploads an image to Amazon S3, without the team managing any servers. Which service should run the thumbnail code?
explanation: Lambda runs code in response to events such as S3 uploads, scales automatically and bills only for execution time. EC2 could run the code but would require the team to provision and manage servers.

stem: A company wants to run Docker containers on Amazon ECS without provisioning, patching or scaling the underlying EC2 instances. Which option should it use?
options: Amazon ECS with the EC2 launch type
explanation: Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers that removes the need to manage servers or clusters of instances. The ECS EC2 launch type still leaves the customer responsible for the EC2 instances in the cluster.

stem: A company needs to track configuration changes to its resources over time and flag security groups that allow unrestricted SSH access. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Config records resource configuration history and evaluates it against rules, such as restricted SSH, to report compliance. CloudTrail logs the API calls but does not evaluate resource configurations against rules.

stem: A company wants to stop paying for idle resources, adopt a consumption model, and attribute spending to teams. Which Well-Architected pillar is this?
explanation: Cost optimization principles include adopting a consumption model, measuring overall efficiency, and analyzing and attributing expenditure. Sustainability also reduces waste, but its goal is environmental impact rather than spending.

stem: A law firm must keep scanned case files for ten years. The files are almost never read, and retrieval within 12 hours is acceptable. Which S3 storage class costs least?
explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive has the lowest storage price, with standard retrievals completed within 12 hours. Glacier Instant Retrieval returns data in milliseconds but stores it at a higher per-GB price than needed here.

stem: An organization already runs its containerized applications on Kubernetes on premises and wants AWS to manage the Kubernetes control plane in the cloud. Which service should it adopt?
explanation: EKS is a managed Kubernetes service that runs the control plane for you and is compatible with standard Kubernetes tooling. ECS is an AWS-native container orchestrator and does not run Kubernetes.

stem: A security team must find out which user changed a security group yesterday and whether the group's settings now break a company rule. Which services provide this information? (Choose two.)
explanation: CloudTrail records the API call, including who made the change and when, and AWS Config records the security group's configuration history and evaluates it against rules. Inspector is tempting because it is a security service, but it scans workloads for software vulnerabilities rather than tracking configuration changes.

stem: A company wants to minimize the environmental impact of its workloads by maximizing utilization and reducing energy consumption. Which pillar addresses this?
explanation: The sustainability pillar, added in 2021, focuses on reducing environmental impact through higher utilization and more efficient hardware and software. Cost optimization often lowers usage too, but it targets spending rather than energy and emissions.

stem: A small bakery with little cloud experience wants to launch a WordPress website on a simple virtual private server for a low, predictable monthly price. Which service is the best fit?
explanation: Lightsail bundles a virtual server, storage, and data transfer into simple fixed monthly plans with preconfigured apps such as WordPress. EC2 offers more flexibility but requires more setup and has less predictable pricing for beginners.

stem: A company wants a managed service to create and control encryption keys that integrates natively with Amazon S3 and Amazon EBS. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS KMS creates and manages encryption keys, integrates with S3, EBS and most other services, and logs key use in CloudTrail. CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware but requires more management and is chosen for single-tenant requirements.

stem: A company wants its architecture to assume that any component can fail at any time and to keep the application running anyway. Which design principle is this?
explanation: Designing for failure means building redundancy and automatic recovery so that no single component failure stops the application. Tightly coupled components do the opposite, because one failure cascades to the others.

stem: A research lab needs to run hundreds of thousands of computing jobs, with AWS queueing the jobs and provisioning the right amount of compute for each. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Batch manages job queues and dynamically provisions the optimal compute resources for large numbers of batch jobs. Lambda suits short event-driven functions and has a 15-minute maximum run time per invocation.

stem: Regulations require a company to store its encryption keys in dedicated single-tenant hardware security modules that it exclusively controls. Which service meets this requirement?
options: AWS KMS with AWS managed keys
explanation: CloudHSM provides dedicated, single-tenant FIPS-validated hardware security modules under the customer's exclusive control. AWS KMS uses HSMs too, but they are multi-tenant and managed by AWS.

stem: An analytics team stores data with unpredictable, changing access patterns and wants storage costs optimized automatically without paying retrieval fees. Which S3 storage class should it choose?
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between access tiers based on use for a small monitoring fee and charges no retrieval fees. Standard-IA and One Zone-IA charge a per-GB retrieval fee, which adds up when access is unpredictable.

stem: Which is a characteristic of serverless compute such as AWS Lambda compared with virtual machines on Amazon EC2?
options: No servers to manage, and you pay only for compute used
You choose, install and patch the guest operating system
You pay hourly for instances even when they sit idle
You must size and manage the cluster's worker nodes
explanation: With serverless compute AWS manages the servers and operating system, and billing is based on requests and execution time. Choosing and patching the operating system is a customer task on EC2 virtual machines, not on Lambda.

stem: A company wants its order service to keep accepting orders even when the downstream fulfillment service is temporarily unavailable. Which approach supports this?
options: Run both services on one large EC2 instance
Connect the services with synchronous API calls
Decouple the services with an Amazon SQS queue
Place both services in the same Availability Zone
explanation: An SQS queue buffers orders so the producer keeps working while the consumer is down, and the consumer processes the backlog when it recovers. Synchronous API calls create tight coupling, so a failed fulfillment service would block order intake.

stem: An application has database passwords hard-coded in its source files. The company wants to store them centrally and rotate them automatically. Which service should it use?
explanation: Secrets Manager stores credentials securely, lets applications retrieve them at runtime and rotates them automatically. KMS manages encryption keys, not application secrets with rotation.

stem: A company is migrating a legacy application that needs full administrative control of the operating system and custom kernel-level software. Which compute service should it use?
explanation: EC2 provides virtual machines where the customer has full control over the operating system and installed software. Lambda, Fargate, and App Runner abstract the operating system away, so custom kernel-level software cannot be installed.

stem: A company is redesigning a tightly coupled application. Which practices make its components more loosely coupled? (Choose two.)
options: Put a message queue between components
Have components share one database schema
Make every call synchronous and blocking
explanation: A queue such as Amazon SQS buffers work between components, and well-defined APIs hide each component's internals, so one can change or fail without breaking the others. A shared database schema may look efficient, but it ties every component to the same data structure, which is tight coupling.

stem: A company needs public SSL/TLS certificates for its Application Load Balancer that are provisioned at no extra cost and renewed automatically. Which service should it use?
explanation: ACM issues public TLS certificates for integrated services such as ELB and CloudFront at no additional cost and renews them automatically. KMS manages encryption keys, not certificates.

stem: A company runs MySQL on self-managed EC2 instances and wants AWS to handle patching, automated backups and Multi-AZ failover while keeping its relational schema. Which service should it move to?
options: MySQL on larger Amazon EC2 instances
explanation: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service that automates patching, backups, and Multi-AZ failover. Staying on EC2 keeps the database self-hosted, so the company would still manage those tasks itself.

stem: An AWS Partner that resells AWS wants to group customer accounts, apply its own pricing rates and produce pro forma bills for each group. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Billing Conductor lets you group accounts, define custom pricing rules and generate pro forma billing data for showback or chargeback. Cost Explorer only analyzes the actual AWS charges and cannot apply custom rates.

stem: A gaming company needs a serverless NoSQL key-value database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale for player profiles. Which service should it choose?
explanation: DynamoDB is a fully managed, serverless key-value and document database with consistent single-digit millisecond latency at any scale. RDS for PostgreSQL is relational and requires choosing and sizing database instances.

stem: Data residency laws require a company to keep customer data inside the European Union. How can the company control where its data is stored on AWS?
options: Deploy resources only in EU Regions
Enable AWS Shield Advanced on all accounts
Ask AWS Support to place the data
Store data in EU edge locations
explanation: Customers choose the Region where content is stored, and AWS does not move it out of that Region without customer action. Edge locations cache content for delivery and are not a data residency control.

stem: A company wants to handle increasing web traffic by adding more EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancer. What type of scaling is this?
explanation: Adding more instances is horizontal scaling (scaling out), which also removes single points of failure. Vertical scaling means moving to a larger instance, which has size limits and keeps one point of failure.

stem: A social network wants to store users and the relationships between them to power friend-of-friend recommendations. Which database service is purpose-built for this?
explanation: Neptune is a managed graph database designed to store and query highly connected data such as social relationships. DocumentDB is a MongoDB-compatible document database and is not optimized for traversing relationships.

stem: A company must show auditors how it protects stored data. Which measures protect data at rest? (Choose three.)
options: Default encryption on an S3 bucket
Encrypting an EBS volume with KMS
Restricting ports in a security group
explanation: S3 default encryption, KMS-encrypted EBS volumes and encrypted RDS storage all protect data where it is stored. TLS and a VPN tunnel are tempting because they encrypt, but they protect data in transit, and a security group filters traffic without encrypting anything.

stem: A company wants to create identical, repeatable environments from templates instead of configuring resources manually in the console. Which AWS service supports this?
explanation: CloudFormation provisions resources from infrastructure-as-code templates, supporting the design principle of performing operations as code. AWS Config records and evaluates resource configurations, but it does not build environments.

stem: Business analysts need to run complex SQL queries across petabytes of historical sales data for reporting and business intelligence. Which AWS service should the company use?
explanation: Redshift is a columnar data warehouse built for analytical SQL queries over very large datasets. RDS is designed for transactional (OLTP) workloads and is not optimized for petabyte-scale analytics.

stem: A team wants an email alert when its forecasted monthly AWS spending is expected to exceed \$5,000. Which service meets this requirement?
explanation: AWS Budgets sends alerts when actual or forecasted cost or usage exceeds a threshold you set. Cost Explorer can show forecasts but does not send alerts, and a CloudWatch billing alarm watches only actual estimated charges.

stem: A company wants to automatically discover sensitive data, such as credit card numbers and personal information, stored in its Amazon S3 buckets. Which service should it use?
explanation: Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to find and report sensitive data such as PII in S3. GuardDuty detects threats from log analysis but does not classify data content.

stem: A company wants to reduce time spent on database patching, backups, and hardware provisioning. Which approach best follows AWS design principles?
options: Install the database software on Amazon EC2 instances
Keep the database on on-premises servers
Use a managed database service such as Amazon RDS
Attach larger EBS volumes to the database server
explanation: Managed services such as Amazon RDS handle patching, backups, and hardware so teams can focus on applications. Running the database on EC2 leaves operating system and database maintenance with the customer.

stem: An application's relational database is overloaded by repeated identical read queries. The company wants to keep frequently accessed results in memory for microsecond responses. Which service should it add?
explanation: ElastiCache provides managed in-memory caching with Redis OSS, Valkey, or Memcached, which offloads repeated reads from the database. CloudFront caches web content at edge locations, not database query results inside the application tier.

stem: A company wants intelligent threat detection that analyzes CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs to find activity such as cryptocurrency mining. Which service fits?
explanation: GuardDuty continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs to detect malicious or unauthorized behavior. Detective helps investigate findings after they occur rather than detecting threats itself.

stem: A company wants to migrate an on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime, including converting the schema. Which AWS tools should it use?
options: AWS DataSync with AWS Snowball Edge
AWS DMS with the AWS Schema Conversion Tool
AWS Storage Gateway with AWS Backup
explanation: The Schema Conversion Tool converts the Oracle schema to PostgreSQL, and DMS replicates the data with continuous replication to minimize downtime. Application Migration Service rehosts whole servers and does not convert a database engine.

stem: A company wants any web server to be replaceable at any time without losing user session data. Which design practice supports this?
options: Keep session data on the local disk of each instance
Store session state externally in Amazon DynamoDB
Assign an Elastic IP address to every server
Increase the size of each web server
explanation: Keeping servers stateless, with session data in a shared store such as DynamoDB or ElastiCache, lets any instance be terminated or replaced. Data on a local disk is lost when the instance is replaced.

stem: A company wants automated, continual scanning of its EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities. Which service should it use?
explanation: Inspector scans EC2, ECR container images and Lambda functions for known software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and unintended network exposure. GuardDuty detects active threats from logs, not software vulnerabilities.

stem: A finance analyst wants to view charts of the last 12 months of spending by service and see a forecast for the coming months. Which tool should the analyst use?
explanation: AWS Cost Explorer provides an interactive view of historical costs, filtering by service, account or tag, and cost forecasts. The Cost and Usage Report is the most detailed data, but it is delivered as raw files rather than ready-made charts.

stem: In an Amazon VPC, what makes a subnet a public subnet?
options: Its route table has a route to an internet gateway
Its network ACL allows all inbound HTTP traffic
Its instances use a security group that allows all ports
It sends outbound traffic through a NAT gateway
explanation: A subnet is public when its associated route table sends internet-bound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) to an internet gateway. A subnet whose default route points to a NAT gateway is a private subnet, and permissive security groups or ACLs do not create a path to the internet.

stem: A company wants to protect its application with controls at the edge, the VPC, the subnet, the instance, and the code. Which security design principle is this?
explanation: Applying security at all layers means defense in depth across edge, network, compute, and application controls. Enabling traceability is also a security principle, but it concerns logging and monitoring actions rather than layered defenses.

stem: A security team wants one place that aggregates findings from GuardDuty, Inspector and Macie and checks accounts against security best practice standards. Which service fits?
explanation: Security Hub aggregates and prioritizes findings from AWS security services and runs automated checks against standards such as the CIS benchmarks. Detective is for investigating root causes, not aggregating posture.

stem: Application servers in a private subnet must download operating system patches from the internet, but must not accept connections initiated from the internet. What should be added?
options: An internet gateway route from the private subnet
A NAT gateway in a public subnet
explanation: A NAT gateway lets instances in private subnets start outbound connections to the internet while blocking connections initiated from outside. Routing the private subnet straight to an internet gateway would make it public and expose the servers.

stem: A company wants to address skills gaps, new job roles, and organizational change management as it moves to the cloud. Which AWS CAF perspective covers this?
explanation: The People perspective bridges technology and business through culture, workforce transformation, and change management. Governance focuses on program and risk management rather than skills and roles.

stem: After GuardDuty reports a suspicious finding, an analyst must investigate its root cause by visualizing related activity over time. Which service should the analyst use?
explanation: Detective builds a linked graph from logs so analysts can investigate the root cause and scope of findings. Security Hub aggregates findings but does not provide that investigation graph.

stem: Which statement correctly compares security groups and network ACLs in an Amazon VPC?
options: Security groups are stateless; network ACLs are stateful
Both operate at the subnet level and support deny rules
Security groups are stateful; network ACLs are stateless
Network ACLs attach to instances; security groups attach to subnets
explanation: Security groups act at the instance (network interface) level, are stateful so return traffic is allowed automatically, and support only allow rules. Network ACLs act at the subnet level, are stateless, and support both allow and deny rules.

stem: Which AWS billing resource delivers the most granular, line-item cost and usage data to an Amazon S3 bucket for querying with Amazon Athena?
explanation: The AWS Cost and Usage Report, now delivered through AWS Data Exports as CUR 2.0, writes the most comprehensive line-item billing data to S3, where Athena, Redshift or QuickSight can analyze it. CloudTrail records API activity, not costs.

stem: A company runs 40 VPCs across several accounts and also connects two on-premises data centers. It wants a central hub instead of managing a full mesh of peering connections. Which service fits?
explanation: Transit Gateway acts as a regional hub that connects many VPCs and on-premises networks through a single gateway. VPC peering is one-to-one and not transitive, so 40 VPCs would need hundreds of separate peering connections.

stem: A company plans to run a penetration test against its own EC2 instances. What does the AWS penetration testing policy require?
options: No prior approval for permitted services
Written approval from AWS Support first
A subscription to AWS Shield Advanced
A request submitted through AWS Artifact
explanation: AWS allows customers to run penetration tests against a list of permitted services, including EC2, without prior approval. Prohibited activities such as DoS flooding are still not allowed.

stem: A company is using the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) to plan its move to the cloud. Which of the following are AWS CAF perspectives? (Choose two.)
explanation: The six AWS CAF perspectives are Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security and Operations. Reliability, sustainability and cost optimization are tempting because they sound like planning areas, but they are pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework, a separate framework.

stem: A company wants to connect its on-premises data center to an Amazon VPC. Which AWS services provide this connection? (Choose two.)
explanation: Site-to-Site VPN builds encrypted tunnels over the internet, and Direct Connect provides a dedicated private link; both connect an on-premises network to a VPC. VPC peering is tempting, but it connects one VPC to another VPC, not to an on-premises network.

stem: A company's public website suffers frequent DDoS attacks and needs 24/7 access to the Shield Response Team plus protection from scaling charges. Which service should it use?
explanation: Shield Advanced adds enhanced DDoS detection, 24/7 Shield Response Team access and cost protection for attack-related scaling. Shield Standard is free and automatic but includes neither the response team nor cost protection.

stem: A company wants to move hundreds of on-premises virtual machines to Amazon EC2 quickly without changing the applications. Which migration strategy should it use?
explanation: Rehosting, or lift and shift, moves applications as they are and is the fastest way to migrate at scale. Refactoring re-architects the application, which takes far more time and effort.

stem: An application is deployed in three AWS Regions, and the company wants Amazon Route 53 to send each user to the Region that responds fastest for them. Which routing policy should it choose?
explanation: Latency-based routing answers DNS queries with the Region that has the lowest measured network latency for the user. Geolocation routing decides by the user's location, which is not always the fastest path.

stem: A company planning a migration wants to estimate the monthly cost of a proposed architecture before creating any AWS resources. Which tool should it use?
explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator models the cost of services you have not deployed yet. Cost Explorer analyzes spending that has already happened, and Compute Optimizer right-sizes resources that are already running.

stem: A company needs to block SQL injection and cross-site scripting requests before they reach its web application behind Amazon CloudFront. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that filters HTTP requests with rules for attacks such as SQL injection and XSS. Shield Standard defends against network-layer DDoS attacks, not application-layer exploits.

stem: A streaming media company wants to cache videos and images at edge locations worldwide so viewers get low-latency delivery. Which AWS service meets this need?
explanation: CloudFront is a content delivery network that caches content at edge locations close to viewers. Global Accelerator also uses the AWS edge network, but it routes TCP and UDP traffic to endpoints and does not cache content.

stem: A company wants to move its self-managed MySQL database to Amazon RDS during migration without changing application code. Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Replatforming (lift, tinker, and shift) makes a few cloud optimizations, such as moving to a managed database, without changing the core architecture. Rehosting would move the database server as it is onto EC2.

stem: A company needs a managed, stateful network firewall with intrusion prevention to filter traffic at the perimeter of its entire VPC. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Network Firewall is a managed service providing stateful inspection and intrusion prevention for VPC traffic. AWS WAF only inspects web (HTTP/HTTPS) requests to specific resources.

stem: Developers want to publish, secure and throttle REST APIs that invoke AWS Lambda functions, including API keys and usage plans for partners. Which service should they use?
explanation: API Gateway creates, publishes and secures REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs, with throttling, API keys and usage plans built in. AppSync is for managed GraphQL APIs, not REST APIs with usage plans.

stem: A company wants to replace its on-premises customer relationship management application with a software as a service (SaaS) product. Which strategy is this?
explanation: Repurchasing means moving to a different product, commonly a SaaS offering, and dropping the existing application. Replatforming keeps the same application while making small optimizations.

stem: A company with many accounts in AWS Organizations wants to centrally configure and enforce AWS WAF rules and security group policies across all accounts. Which service fits?
explanation: Firewall Manager centrally manages WAF rules, Shield Advanced, security group policies and Network Firewall across accounts in an organization. Network Firewall is the firewall itself, not the cross-account policy manager.

stem: A company needs a managed relational database for a transactional order system that uses SQL joins. Which AWS services fit? (Choose two.)
explanation: Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS are managed relational database services for transactional SQL workloads. DynamoDB is tempting because it is fully managed and fast, but it is a NoSQL key-value database without joins; Neptune is a graph database and DocumentDB a document database.

stem: A company with 15 AWS accounts turns on consolidated billing in AWS Organizations. Which benefits does it gain? (Choose two.)
options: One bill for all member accounts
Free Business Support for every account
Separate bills for each IAM user
explanation: Consolidated billing gives one bill for the organization and combines usage across accounts, so tiered prices and Reserved Instance or Savings Plans discounts apply more widely. It does not include a Support plan, which is still purchased and billed per account.

stem: A company wants to re-architect a monolithic application into serverless microservices to add features and improve scalability. Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Refactoring (re-architecting) changes how the application is built to use cloud-native features, driven by needs that are hard to meet in the current design. Replatforming makes only minor optimizations without changing the architecture.

stem: A company wants to control who can read objects in its Amazon S3 buckets. Which features control access to S3 data? (Choose two.)
explanation: Bucket policies grant or deny access to a bucket and its objects, and Block Public Access overrides any setting that would make data public. Lifecycle rules are tempting because they act on objects automatically, but they manage storage class and expiry, not who can read the data.

stem: Which Amazon S3 storage classes keep data in a single Availability Zone? (Choose two.)
explanation: S3 One Zone-IA and S3 Express One Zone store data in one Availability Zone, trading AZ-level resilience for lower cost or, with Express One Zone, single-digit millisecond access. S3 Intelligent-Tiering is tempting because it moves data to cheaper tiers, but like S3 Standard and Glacier Deep Archive it stores data across at least three Availability Zones.

stem: Audit records must be kept for ten years, are almost never read, and a retrieval time of up to 48 hours is acceptable. Which S3 storage class has the lowest storage cost?
explanation: Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost S3 storage class, built for long-term retention with retrievals within 12 to 48 hours. Glacier Flexible Retrieval restores data faster but costs more to store.

stem: A company must block a specific malicious IP address range from reaching every instance in a subnet. Which VPC feature should it use?
explanation: Network ACLs apply at the subnet level and support explicit deny rules, so they can block an IP range. Security groups support only allow rules, so they cannot explicitly deny an address.

stem: A company has finished planning its migration. Which AWS services copy its on-premises servers and databases into AWS? (Choose two.)
explanation: AWS Application Migration Service replicates servers for a lift-and-shift cutover, and AWS DMS migrates databases while the source stays online. Application Discovery Service is tempting because it is a migration tool, but it only collects server and dependency data for planning and does not move workloads.

stem: Log files in an S3 bucket should move to a cheaper storage class after 30 days and be deleted automatically after one year. Which S3 feature does this?
explanation: Lifecycle rules transition objects to other storage classes and expire them after set periods. Versioning keeps prior versions of objects but does not move or delete them on a schedule.

stem: A company wants its billing reports to break down AWS costs by department and project. What should the company do?
options: Create a separate VPC per department
explanation: After resources are tagged and the tags are activated as cost allocation tags, Cost Explorer and the Cost and Usage Report can group costs by those tags. VPCs and IAM groups organize networking and permissions, not billing data.

stem: A company wants free automated checks that flag security groups with unrestricted ports and confirm that MFA is enabled on the root user. Which service provides these?
explanation: Trusted Advisor core security checks, free for all accounts, include unrestricted security group ports and root user MFA. Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities rather than account configuration best practices.

stem: A company wants to gather server specifications, utilization data, and dependencies from its on-premises data center to plan a migration. Which AWS service helps?
explanation: Application Discovery Service collects configuration, usage, and dependency data from on-premises servers to help plan migrations. Application Migration Service performs the actual lift-and-shift replication after planning.

stem: Regulators require that trade records be stored in a write-once-read-many (WORM) model so that no one, even an administrator, can delete them during retention. Which feature meets this?
options: S3 Versioning with MFA Delete enabled
S3 Object Lock in compliance mode
explanation: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode enforces WORM retention, so no user, including the root user, can delete or overwrite a protected version until retention expires. Versioning with MFA Delete makes deletion harder, but an authorized user with MFA can still delete versions.

stem: An administrator must give twelve developers identical permissions and be able to change them all at once later. What is the most efficient approach?
options: Attach the same inline policy to each user
Share one IAM user's credentials among them
Add the users to an IAM group with a policy
Give each developer the root user password
explanation: Attaching a policy to an IAM group grants it to every member, and one change updates them all. Separate inline policies must be edited user by user, and shared credentials break accountability.

stem: A self-managed database on one EC2 instance needs low-latency block storage that persists when the instance stops and can be backed up with point-in-time snapshots. Which option fits?
explanation: EBS provides persistent block storage attached to an EC2 instance, and EBS snapshots give incremental point-in-time backups stored in S3. Instance store is also block storage, but its data is lost when the instance stops or terminates.

stem: A company wants to lift and shift physical and virtual servers to AWS with continuous block-level replication and minimal cutover downtime. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) continuously replicates source servers to AWS and launches them with short cutover windows, making it the recommended rehost tool. Application Discovery Service only collects planning data and does not move servers.

stem: An application running on Amazon EC2 needs to read objects from an S3 bucket. What is the most secure way to grant this access?
options: Store an IAM user's access keys on the instance
Embed root user access keys in the code
Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance
explanation: An IAM role attached through an instance profile supplies temporary, automatically rotated credentials to the application. Storing long-term access keys on the instance risks leaking them.

stem: Hundreds of Linux EC2 instances in several Availability Zones must read and write the same files at once through NFS, and capacity should grow automatically. Which service should be used?
options: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
explanation: Amazon EFS is a managed, elastic NFS file system that many Linux instances across multiple Availability Zones can mount at the same time. An EBS volume is block storage normally attached to a single instance in one Availability Zone, and FSx for Windows File Server serves SMB shares to Windows clients.

stem: A company wants to be notified automatically when its spending pattern suddenly deviates from normal, using machine learning to detect the change. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to spot unusual spending and sends alerts with root-cause details. A CloudWatch billing alarm fires only when charges cross a fixed threshold, and Compute Optimizer gives right-sizing advice.

stem: Which statement describes the principle of least privilege?
options: Grant administrator access, then trim it during audits
Give every user read-only access to all services
Grant only the permissions required for a task
Grant permissions based on each user's seniority
explanation: Least privilege means granting only the permissions needed to perform a task, and nothing more. Starting broad and trimming later leaves excess access in place in the meantime.

stem: A company wants to migrate an Oracle database to Amazon Aurora while keeping the source database fully operational during the migration. Which service should it use?
explanation: AWS DMS migrates databases while the source stays operational and supports heterogeneous migrations, with the Schema Conversion Tool converting the schema. DataSync copies files and objects, not live database changes.

stem: Many Amazon EC2 instances must mount the same shared file system at the same time. Which AWS services provide this managed file storage? (Choose two.)
explanation: Amazon EFS and the Amazon FSx family (for Windows File Server, Lustre, NetApp ONTAP and OpenZFS) are managed file systems that many instances can mount at once. An EBS volume is tempting because it is fast, but it is block storage attached to a single instance, and gp3 volumes do not support Multi-Attach.

stem: A company has just created a new AWS account. Which actions follow best practice for the root user? (Choose two.)
options: Enable MFA on the root user
Create root access keys for scripts
Share the root password with admins
Use it only for tasks that need it
explanation: AWS recommends protecting the root user with MFA and using it only for the few tasks that require it, with IAM identities for everything else. Root access keys for scripts may seem convenient, but they give unrestricted long-term access and should not exist.

stem: On-premises applications must keep writing to local NFS and SMB file shares while the files are stored durably in Amazon S3, with frequently used data cached locally. Which service fits?
explanation: Storage Gateway (S3 File Gateway) presents local file shares and stores files as objects in S3, with a local cache for low-latency access. Direct Connect is only a network link and does not provide file shares.

stem: A company that already orders AWS Snowball Edge devices wants to move 500 TB of archived data to AWS, but its internet connection would take months to transfer it. Which service should it use?
explanation: Snowball Edge devices move large datasets physically, which is faster than a slow network for hundreds of terabytes; since November 2025 only existing customers can order them. S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads over the internet but still depends on the limited connection.

stem: In a standalone AWS account, which task requires signing in as the root user?
explanation: Closing a standalone account is one of the few tasks that require root user credentials. Creating groups, launching instances and viewing CloudTrail history can be granted to IAM identities.

stem: A company wants one central policy to schedule and retain backups of its EBS volumes, RDS databases, DynamoDB tables and EFS file systems across accounts. What should it use?
explanation: AWS Backup centrally manages and automates backup plans and retention across many AWS services and accounts. Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates servers for fast failover; it is not a policy-based backup service for databases and file systems.

stem: A company needs a designated Technical Account Manager and a 15-minute response for business-critical outages, at the lowest cost. Which Support plan should it choose?
explanation: Enterprise Support assigns a designated Technical Account Manager and targets a 15-minute response for business-critical outages. Business Support+ costs less, but its fastest response target is 30 minutes and it does not include a designated TAM.

stem: An employee uses the AWS CLI on a workstation to call AWS APIs with long-term IAM user credentials. Which credential type does the CLI require?
options: A console user name and password
An access key ID and secret access key
explanation: Programmatic access through the CLI, SDKs or APIs uses an access key ID and secret access key. A console password only signs in to the AWS Management Console, and EC2 key pairs are for logging in to instances.

stem: A company wants to automate recurring online transfers of files from on-premises NFS shares to Amazon S3 and Amazon EFS. Which service should it use?
explanation: DataSync automates and accelerates online data movement between on-premises storage such as NFS or SMB shares and AWS storage services. Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, FTPS, and FTP endpoints for partners, not scheduled bulk copies from file shares.

stem: A social media startup wants to detect faces, objects and unsafe content in user-uploaded photos without building or training its own machine learning models. Which service fits?
explanation: Rekognition is a pretrained image and video analysis service that detects faces, objects and inappropriate content through an API. SageMaker could do this too, but the team would have to build, train and host its own models.

stem: A company with 40 AWS accounts wants employees to sign in once with their corporate directory credentials and reach their assigned accounts. Which service should it use?
explanation: IAM Identity Center provides single sign-on for workforce users across all accounts in an organization and connects to existing identity providers. Cognito is designed for customers of applications, not employees.

stem: An insurer receives thousands of scanned claim forms and wants to automatically extract printed text, handwriting, tables and form fields. Which AWS service should it use?
explanation: Textract extracts text, handwriting, tables and key-value form data from scanned documents. Rekognition can find text in images, but it does not understand document structure such as forms and tables.

stem: A company is comparing on-premises costs with AWS. Which of these is a fixed, upfront expense in a traditional data center?
options: Paying per second for EC2 instance usage
Paying per gigabyte of Amazon S3 storage used
Buying physical servers and storage arrays
Paying per request for AWS Lambda functions
explanation: Hardware purchases are capital expenditures paid upfront regardless of later usage, which makes them a fixed cost. EC2, S3, and Lambda charges are variable costs that track actual consumption.

stem: A mobile app needs sign-up and sign-in for millions of customers, including sign-in through social identity providers. Which AWS service should the developers use?
explanation: Cognito provides user sign-up, sign-in and federation with social providers for web and mobile app users at scale. IAM Identity Center manages workforce access to AWS accounts, not app customers.

stem: A retailer wants to analyze thousands of written product reviews to find customer sentiment and key phrases using natural language processing. Which service should it choose?
explanation: Comprehend is a natural language processing service that identifies sentiment, key phrases, entities and language in text. Transcribe converts speech to text and does not analyze sentiment in written reviews.

stem: A new AWS account has not purchased any Support plan. Which Support plan does it already have at no extra cost?
explanation: Basic Support comes with every AWS account and covers account and billing customer service, documentation, AWS re:Post, AWS Health and the core Trusted Advisor checks. Developer Support is tempting as the entry-level plan, but it is a paid plan.

stem: A company finds that its Amazon EC2 instances average 5 percent CPU utilization all month. Which cost optimization action should it take first?
options: Add more instances to the Auto Scaling group
Move the instances to Dedicated Hosts
Migrate the same instances to a different AWS Region for lower prices
Right-size the instances to smaller instance types
explanation: Right-sizing matches instance types to actual workload needs, and AWS Compute Optimizer recommends smaller sizes for underused instances. Adding instances would increase spending on capacity that is already idle.

stem: An auditing firm needs temporary access to resources in a company's AWS account without the company creating IAM users for it. What should the company configure?
options: An IAM user with shared access keys
The root user credentials protected by MFA
A security group allowing the firm's IP
A cross-account IAM role the firm can assume
explanation: A cross-account role lets identities in another account assume it and receive temporary credentials. Shared access keys are long-term, hard to audit and against best practice.

stem: A call center wants to convert recorded customer calls into text and then translate that text into Spanish. Which AWS services should it use? (Choose two.)
explanation: Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text, and Amazon Translate translates text between languages. Amazon Polly is tempting because it works with speech, but it does the reverse, turning text into spoken audio.

stem: To build a generative AI application, a team wants API access to foundation models from several providers without training models or managing any infrastructure. Which service fits best?
explanation: Bedrock is a fully managed, serverless service that offers foundation models from Amazon and other providers through one API. SageMaker is for building, training and deploying your own models, which involves more ML expertise and infrastructure choices.

stem: Which AWS service issues the temporary security credentials provided when an IAM role is assumed?
explanation: AWS STS issues short-lived credentials when a role is assumed or a federated user signs in. Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets but does not issue role credentials.

stem: A company wants to use its existing Microsoft Windows Server and SQL Server licenses on AWS to reduce costs. Which licensing approach supports this?
explanation: BYOL lets a company apply licenses it already owns, often on Dedicated Hosts, and AWS License Manager helps track them. License-included instances bundle the license cost into the hourly price, so the company would pay for licenses twice.

stem: Analysts want to run standard SQL queries directly against CSV and Parquet files in Amazon S3, paying per query with no servers or clusters to manage. Which service should they use?
explanation: Athena is a serverless, interactive query service that runs SQL on data in S3 and charges per amount of data scanned. EMR runs big data frameworks such as Spark on clusters that must be sized and managed.

stem: Which AWS Enterprise Support feature gives customers a team of billing and account experts for non-technical billing questions?
explanation: The Concierge Support Team, included in Enterprise Support, handles billing and account questions. The Technical Account Manager is the customer's technical advocate for architecture and operations, not billing.

stem: A company's AWS Lambda function must write logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs and read from DynamoDB. How should the company grant these permissions?
options: An execution role the function assumes
An IAM user with access keys for the function
A resource tag on the log group
A network ACL allowing the function
explanation: AWS services act on a customer's behalf through service roles, and Lambda uses an execution role for its permissions. Long-term IAM user keys in a function are unnecessary and riskier.

stem: A company wants to cut costs by automatically stopping its development EC2 instances every night and weekend. Which approach should it use?
options: Purchase three-year Reserved Instances for development
Move the development instances to Dedicated Hosts
Increase the instance sizes to finish work faster
Automate stop and start schedules for the instances
explanation: Automation such as Instance Scheduler on AWS or Systems Manager stops instances when no one needs them, so the company pays nothing for compute while they are off. Reserved Instances bill for the full term whether or not the instances run, which suits steady workloads rather than part-time ones.

stem: An e-commerce site must ingest and process millions of clickstream events per second in real time for live analytics. Which AWS service is designed for this?
explanation: Kinesis Data Streams captures and processes large streams of data records in real time. Glue is a serverless ETL and data catalog service for batch preparation of data, not real-time stream ingestion.

stem: A security team requires every IAM user password to be at least 14 characters and include symbols. Which feature enforces this requirement?
explanation: The IAM account password policy sets length, complexity and rotation rules for IAM user passwords. An AWS Config rule can report whether such a policy exists, but it does not enforce password complexity.

stem: Business managers need interactive dashboards and visualizations of sales data, with machine learning insights, which they can share across the company. Which AWS service should be used?
explanation: QuickSight is a cloud business intelligence service for building and sharing interactive dashboards. Data Exchange is for finding and subscribing to third-party data sets, not for visualizing them.

stem: When estimating total cost of ownership, which cost does a company typically reduce by moving a self-managed database to Amazon RDS?
options: Data transfer charges for traffic out to the internet
Per-gigabyte charges for stored database data
Staff time for patching, backups, and maintenance
Monthly fees for an AWS Support plan
explanation: Managed services take over undifferentiated operational tasks, lowering labor costs that are a large part of TCO. Data transfer out is still charged whether the database is self-managed or on RDS.

stem: A company using AWS Organizations must stop all member accounts, including their administrators, from using AWS Regions outside Europe. Which feature should it use?
explanation: SCPs set guardrails on the maximum permissions in member accounts, so they can deny actions in disallowed Regions even for administrators. Permission sets grant access to users but cannot restrict an account's administrators.

stem: A company wants its application components to exchange messages so they are decoupled from each other. Which AWS services are designed for this? (Choose two.)
explanation: Amazon SQS queues messages until a consumer processes them, and Amazon SNS publishes messages to many subscribers, so senders and receivers do not call each other directly. AWS Glue is tempting because it moves data between systems, but it is a batch ETL service, not a messaging layer.
