stem: A finance team wants to understand what the company has already spent on AWS. Which tools provide data on past spending? (Choose two.)
explanation: Cost Explorer charts historical costs and usage, and the Cost and Usage Report (now delivered through AWS Data Exports) gives line-item detail of past charges. Pricing Calculator is tempting because it shows costs, but it estimates architectures that have not been deployed yet, and Compute Optimizer reports utilization rather than spending.

stem: Which statement about service control policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations is correct?
options: They grant permissions to users in member accounts
They replace IAM policies in member accounts
They can be attached only to individual IAM users
They limit maximum permissions and grant none
explanation: SCPs define the maximum available permissions for accounts or OUs but never grant access themselves. IAM policies are still needed to grant permissions within those limits.

stem: A company is building a total cost of ownership (TCO) comparison. Which costs belong on the on-premises side of the comparison? (Choose three.)
explanation: An on-premises TCO includes power and cooling, facility space and periodic hardware refreshes, along with staff time. Compute is a large cost on both sides, but per-second EC2 charges are an AWS cost, as are S3 requests and Support plan fees.

stem: A team must coordinate several Lambda functions into a visual workflow with sequencing, branching, retries and error handling. Which AWS service provides this orchestration?
explanation: Step Functions orchestrates multiple services into state-machine workflows with built-in branching, retries and error handling. EventBridge routes events between services but does not manage a multi-step workflow.

stem: A company wants a second layer of protection for IAM user console sign-ins in case a password is stolen. What should it enable?
explanation: MFA requires a second factor, such as an authenticator app or security key, so a stolen password alone is not enough. A stronger password policy still relies on a single factor.

stem: Every time developers push code, a company wants to automatically build, test and deploy the application through defined release stages. Which service orchestrates this release process?
explanation: CodePipeline is a continuous delivery service that models and automates the release stages from source through build, test and deploy. CodeBuild only compiles and tests code, and CodeDeploy only handles the deployment step.

stem: A company wants to compare the full cost of running workloads on premises against AWS, including hardware, facilities, and staff. Which concept should it evaluate?
explanation: TCO captures both direct and indirect costs, including hardware, facilities, power, and labor, over the life of the workload. RPO and RTO are disaster recovery targets, not cost measures.

stem: An auditor needs a list of all IAM users showing the status of their passwords, access keys and MFA devices. What should the administrator provide?
explanation: The IAM credential report lists every user and the status of their passwords, access keys and MFA devices. AWS Artifact holds AWS's compliance reports, not account credential details.

stem: An operations team wants an alert sent when average CPU usage on its EC2 instances stays above 80 percent for 10 minutes. Which service should it use?
explanation: CloudWatch collects metrics such as CPU utilization and uses alarms to trigger notifications or actions when thresholds are crossed. CloudTrail records API activity for auditing and does not monitor performance metrics.

stem: A company wants to buy a third-party firewall appliance, deploy it in minutes and pay for it through its AWS bill. Which resource should it use?
explanation: AWS Marketplace is a curated catalog of third-party software that can be deployed quickly and billed through the AWS account. The Partner Network is a program for consulting and technology partners, not a software storefront.

stem: A security engineer wants to keep up with new AWS security features, best practices and solutions written by AWS security experts. Which resource should the engineer follow?
explanation: The AWS Security Blog publishes security announcements, best practices and solution walkthroughs by AWS experts. The AWS Health Dashboard reports service events affecting accounts, not guidance articles.

stem: A company wants the lowest compute cost for fault-tolerant batch jobs that can be stopped and restarted at any time. Which pricing model fits best?
explanation: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at up to 90 percent off On-Demand prices but can be interrupted with a two-minute warning, which batch jobs can tolerate. Reserved Instances require a one- or three-year commitment and suit steady workloads instead.

stem: An administrator needs to patch and run commands on a fleet of EC2 instances and on-premises servers without opening SSH ports or using bastion hosts. What should be used?
explanation: Systems Manager provides Patch Manager, Run Command and Session Manager to operate EC2 and on-premises servers without inbound SSH. Inspector finds software vulnerabilities but does not apply patches.

stem: A developer has a question about securing an S3 bucket and wants answers from the AWS community and AWS experts in a Q&A forum. Which resource fits?
explanation: AWS re:Post is the community Q&A service where AWS experts and users answer questions, and it also hosts Knowledge Center articles. Trusted Advisor runs automated checks rather than answering questions.

stem: A company with remote staff wants managed, persistent Windows and Linux virtual desktops that employees can reach from any device. Which AWS service meets this need?
explanation: WorkSpaces is a managed desktop-as-a-service offering persistent virtual desktops. WorkSpaces Applications (formerly AppStream 2.0) streams individual applications to a browser instead of providing a full persistent desktop.

stem: A company's application runs on Amazon EC2 at a steady level around the clock and must not be interrupted for the next three years. Which purchase options lower its cost in exchange for a commitment? (Choose two.)
explanation: Compute Savings Plans (up to 66 percent off) and Standard Reserved Instances (up to 72 percent off) both trade a 1- or 3-year commitment for a discount on steady usage. Spot Instances can be cheaper still, but AWS can reclaim them with a two-minute warning, and On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve capacity at the full On-Demand price.

stem: A security team is writing rules for identity management in its AWS accounts. Which practices follow IAM security best practices? (Choose three.)
options: Share access keys within each team
Embed access keys in application code
Use IAM roles for workloads on AWS
explanation: Least privilege, MFA for people and IAM roles with temporary credentials for workloads are core IAM best practices. Giving developers administrator access can look like a time saver, but it breaks least privilege, and shared or embedded access keys are long-term credentials that leak easily.

stem: Thousands of factory sensors must securely connect to AWS and publish telemetry using MQTT, with rules that route the messages to other services. Which service should be used?
explanation: IoT Core securely connects devices to AWS over protocols such as MQTT and routes their messages to other services with rules. SNS is a pub/sub notification service for applications and does not manage device connections or identity.

stem: A company notices that an Amazon EC2 instance in another AWS account is sending spam and port scans to its servers. Whom should the company report this to?
explanation: The AWS Abuse team (AWS Trust & Safety) investigates reports of AWS resources used for spam, port scanning, DDoS or other abuse. AWS Health Dashboard shows service events affecting your own account and does not take abuse reports.

stem: A company is launching a short-term project with unpredictable usage that cannot be interrupted and does not allow any long-term commitment. Which pricing model fits?
explanation: On-Demand Instances need no commitment and run until the company stops them, which suits short, unpredictable workloads. Savings Plans and Reserved Instances require one- or three-year commitments, and Spot Instances can be interrupted.

stem: A company lacks in-house security expertise and wants experts to help design and build its cloud security architecture. Which options provide this hands-on help? (Choose two.)
explanation: AWS Professional Services and consulting firms in the AWS Partner Network provide experts who design and implement solutions with the customer. Trusted Advisor is tempting because it gives security recommendations, but its automated checks do not design or build anything, and re:Post offers community answers only.

stem: Front-end developers want to quickly build, host and deploy a full-stack web and mobile app with built-in authentication and CI/CD, with little backend expertise. Which service fits best?
explanation: Amplify gives front-end developers tools and managed hosting to build, connect and deploy full-stack web and mobile apps. AppSync is only a managed GraphQL API layer, and Device Farm tests apps on real devices.
